The role

Due process starts at a door. Before a lawsuit can move forward, the person being sued has to be properly notified, and for thousands of cases every day, that happens through a process server using our mobile app. It's one of the most critical steps in the litigation system.

As a Product Manager on the Server Experience and Fulfilment team, you'll own the product experience that helps those servers get it right and on time, from understanding requirements and planning attempts to capturing reliable evidence of service. Your goal is to make that work easier for servers, more predictable for the law firms relying on it, and more profitable for our marketplace overall.

What you'll own

• Planning and attempts. How servers plan their day, sequence attempts, work high-volume addresses, and see which jobs are at risk before a deadline passes.

• Evidence of service. The capture and verification behind every attempt: location, time, photos, eligibility checks. Raise the quality bar without slowing servers down, even with no signal.
• Fewer handoffs. Deciding what belongs in the app, what AI and automation can handle, and what still needs one of our service specialists.
• Efficient dispatch. How job offers get packaged, priced, and distributed to servers, and the product systems behind server pay.

Your team and scope

You're joining an established team that has driven some of Proof's biggest wins over the last two years. It moves quickly, ships with impact, and has built a best-in-class mobile app for process servers.

You'll report to the CPO and, as a hands-on IC, partner with a dedicated engineering squad and our design team on discovery, analysis, and delivery. • More jobs meet their service deadlines, without more avoidable reattempts.

FlowFuse is the enterprise platform that bridges physical assets and enterprise IT. Built on Node-RED, it lets industrial teams unify real-time data through workflows, AI agents, and industrial applications, extending rigid vendor systems with a low-code agility layer that adapts without rip-and-replace. Our customers run factories, energy grids, and supply chains on what we ship. When we get the platform wrong, a production line feels it.

We need someone to own the FlowFuse platform outright: the solution-agnostic foundation every customer solution is built on. That means enterprise management, edge and cloud deployment, industrial connectivity, industrial data modeling and contextualization, security, operator experience, and the reusable AI/ML capabilities that will set us apart. You decide where the platform goes over the next few years, and you write the work that gets it there.

This is not a roadmap-from-30,000-feet job. You will learn our customers and the industrial IoT (IIoT) space cold, then turn that knowledge into shipped platform capabilities that customers and our Solutions Engineering team reuse instead of rebuilding. You own the platform end to end: vision, roadmap, backlog, prioritization, refinement, and the GitHub issues your engineers actually build from. The tickets have to be exacting and technical. The work is hands-on and often unglamorous. You do it yourself before you ever hand it off.

If that sounds like the part of Product you'd rather skip, this isn't the role. If it sounds like the part you've been missing, keep reading.

What you'll actually do

• Own the platform roadmap. Hold the multi-year, solution-agnostic view, then break it into work that ships this sprint. Decide where to invest beyond today's customer requests, and what to build, integrate, or source through partners. Track where industrial software and our competitors are heading, and decide where FlowFuse can establish meaningful differentiation.

• Run the field-to-platform loop. Partner with Solutions Engineering to spot product gaps and recurring patterns in customer deployments. Decide what becomes a platform capability, what stays in the solution library, and what remains customer-specific. The goal: field-developed work becomes repeatable enterprise solutions, not unicorns we rebuild for every customer.

• Learn our customers and the IIoT domain fast, then keep learning. Run continuous discovery. Sit in on sales and customer calls, mine the recordings in Fathom for the problem behind the request, and talk to users directly.

• Make industrial data a first-class part of the platform. Lead the direction for industrial data modeling and contextualization: data models defined once and enforced across instances and sites, and the relationships between machines, processes, production events, decisions, and outcomes that our workflows and AI build on. AI readiness starts here.

• Shape AI/ML in the platform. Lead the product direction for reusable AI/ML capabilities (AI-assisted development, agentic workflows, industrial data reasoning, machine vision integration), with clear judgment about what's production-ready versus a promising demo.

• Make the platform enterprise-ready. Make it easier for customers and solution engineers to build, deploy, govern, and operate distributed Node-RED applications across many sites, mixed equipment, and cloud or self-hosted environments.

• Run the lane day to day. Triage the backlog and every new idea that flies in, prioritize ruthlessly, sequence it, and get it into sprints.

• Write GitHub issues your engineers respect. Precise, technical, unambiguous, with testable acceptance criteria. They should never have to guess what "done" means.

• Run refinement with engineering. Show up prepared, make the calls, unblock fast, and validate outcomes after release.

• Know the split. Product owns the roadmap, the what, and the why, and writes the issues. Engineering owns the how, technical design, and delivery estimates. Scope and sequencing tradeoffs are made together. There's no classic PM / designer / engineer trio here. It's mostly you and the engineers.

The harder part of the job

Leadership here moves fast and thinks out loud. Ideas arrive at high volume and high velocity, from the CEO, our investors, your peers, and the live customer deals sales is racing to close. Part of the job is to be the filter and the translation layer. Absorb that energy, turn it into a clear and sequenced plan, and protect the engineering team's focus so they can do their best work. You don't pass chaos through. You stop it at your desk.

You'll partner closely with Solutions Engineering, who own customer solutions, industry-specific applications, and solution packaging. They are your most important internal customer. A big part of being effective is turning their field requests into platform capabilities that serve many solutions, not one, without the team feeling whiplash.

You'll also work with our CTO on technical direction and the Node-RED ecosystem. The CTO leads the Node-RED open-source project. You can advocate for upstream changes, but you don't own that project.

You report to the VP of Engineering and Product. You work with the engineering team, not against it. Earning their trust is the job, not a nice-to-have.

You're the person everyone goes to for the state of the platform.
